svg.title: How Filter Stacking Shrinks a Land List
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-list-size-by-pull; chapter number: 4; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: How Filter Stacking Shrinks a Land List; subtitle: Reported record counts from raw county pull to tagged small-town export; caption: Stacking public-record filters cut 82,328 Lehigh Acres lots to 1,250, while priced and tagged exports land in the hundreds or dozens before a dollar goes to mail.; assumptions note: Each bucket is a separate reported pull from a different operator and market; buckets are compared side by side, not summed.; note: Attributed to PropStream testimony on Lehigh Acres, Max Edson of PRYCD (7jGQIvwqBwc), and Seth Williams of REtipster (oJpqcR4iFy8).; total range: 20 to 82,328 records per pull; buckets: label: Lehigh Acres Raw Lots; low: 82328; high: 82328; notes: Unfiltered lot count before the PropStream filter stack.; label: Lehigh Acres After Filter Stack; low: 1250; high: 1250; notes: Raw land isolated by setting improvement value to zero plus stacked owner filters.; label: PRYCD Priced List; low: 300; high: 300; notes: 300 records for $24 with offer price at a 25% default slider.; label: Small-Town Tagged Export; low: 20; high: 40; notes: Apply tags, switch to Less Map, and export about 20 to 40 properties.
